(Northbeam Circle Membership), 67 published documents under `env/env_0005_consumer_electronics_retailer/docs/membership/`.
Source side: `env/env_0005_consumer_electronics_retailer/tasks/membership_benefits_desk/membership.extended.yaml`
(13 base `policies`, 6 `extended_policies`, 59 `parameter_schema` keys, 6 `variants`) and `task_tools.py`
beside it. Blind phase frozen first at
`env/env_0005_consumer_electronics_retailer/audits/runtime_context/membership_benefits_desk/0.md`.

**Entry conditions (checked and cited, not re-run by me).** The difficulty's policy-side verdict PASSED after
three rounds, both tasks on all four relationships, reports at
`env/env_0005_consumer_electronics_retailer/audits/policy_task/membership_benefits_desk/` (not read during the blind
phase). The gate snapshot came with the brief:

All six are present, all six are written as retired, and each retirement sits in the document of the base
policy the source names. The figures those clauses carried are preserved as figures — *"The stacking basis and
the yearly redemption allowance recorded for each tier remain figures of the tier"*, *"The four named benefit
credit figures and the credit life recorded for each tier remain figures of the tier"* — matching the source,
which keeps them in `variants`. No clause is retired that the source's `overwrite` did not declare retired, and
the unnamed clauses of all four affected base policies are still carried as clauses in force (checked
individually: three surviving clauses of `membership_benefit_redemption`, two of `membership_points_accrual`,
five of `membership_points_expiry`, four of `membership_benefit_grant_cycle`, four of
`membership_combo_protection_interaction`, seven of `membership_dues_delinquency`).

**The reconciliation the brief asked about (item 2, first observation).** `membership_ext_benefit_credit_application`
declares retired the base clause naming the credit-to-charge-kind mapping, and its **own `rule`** then contains
that same mapping in a different role: *"The named benefit a charge's kind calls for is the service credit where
the charge is bench or on-site repair labour, the installation credit where it is installation labour, the
delivery credit where it is a delivery charge and the haul-away credit where it is a haul-away charge."* The
renderer put the retired clause in `circle_benefit_credit_spending_rules_dfad59cd` (as retired) and the live
mapping in `circle_benefit_credit_amount_determination_f1ec47a8` §3. **That is exactly what the source has, on
both sides, in the right documents.** It is not two readings of one rule: the retired clause was a
*restriction* on what a credit may be spent against; the surviving sentence is a *selector* fixing which named
benefit's standing is read. Nothing in the corpus offers the solver a choice — `circle_benefit_credit_amount_determination_f1ec47a8`
§1 says the amount is *"the credit standing under the named benefit that charge's kind calls for"*, so for the
repair-labour charge `TW-5188-0914` the named benefit is the service credit and no other. The blind derivation
reached that without hesitation, and reached the GT figure. **Faithful; the renderer's decision was correct.**

### F. Each `prerequisite`, listed separately

**Edge 1 — `membership_ext_benefit_credit_application` waits on `membership_ext_year_benefit_credit_grant`.**
`kind value_input`, `gate credit_standing`, `form state`.

- `policy_source`: *"The credit set against a charge is worked out only after the ledger carries, for the
  membership year in which that charge falls, a grant of the very named benefit that charge's kind calls for."*
- Carried **verbatim**, ordering connective (*"only after"*) and form intact, in the blocked policy's own hub
  `circle_benefit_credit_application_request_deb961b6`, under the heading *"When the amount set against a
  charge is worked out"*. A search of all 385 published documents finds that sentence in **that document
  alone**.
- Form honoured: the sentence names a record-visible **state** (a grant entry standing on the ledger for a
  membership year) and names no action, no performer, no tool, no policy and no document.
- Resolution basis, at the source's strength: the state is identified from the sentence plus
  `circle_benefit_credit_amount_determination_f1ec47a8` §3 (repair labour → the service credit) and the
  membership record's `current_term_start 2026-09-01` (the membership year → 2026); its absence is read from
  `find_membership_events`, whose `grant_cycle_year 2026` rows carry `install_credit` and `delivery_credit`
  only; and the write that brings it about is found from the words the records use (`membership_benefit_grant`,
  `benefit_code`, `grant_cycle_year`) in the depended-on policy's own documents,
  `circle_year_benefit_credit_grant_entry_4d4d5404` (*"it is granted once for that year under the service
  credit"*, *"The membership ledger gains a grant entry carrying the named benefit, the membership year it is
  granted for, the credit money and the tier"*) and `circle_year_credit_determination_46757041`.
- Strength matches: a hard gate on the source side (`gate credit_standing`, whose binding is held to nothing
  until the state holds) and a hard gate in the prose (*"is worked out only after"*), neither optional nor
  advisable nor combinable.
- The depended-on side discloses nothing: neither `circle_year_benefit_credit_grant_entry_4d4d5404` nor any
  document of the grant policy carries this sentence or mentions who waits on it.
- `condition`, `resolved_by` (`grant_benefit_credit_b1d93258`) and `effect` appear in **no** document.
  Verified: that tool name occurs in exactly one document, its own hub.

**Edge 2 — `membership_ext_year_benefit_credit_grant` waits on `membership_ext_grace_dues_settlement`.**
`kind value_input`, `gate dues_standing_adjustment`, `form state`.

- `policy_source`: *"The credit granted for a membership year is worked out only after the dues charged for the
  billing period the membership is now in stand met in full by the payments applied to that period."*
- Carried **verbatim** in the blocked policy's own hub `circle_year_benefit_credit_grant_entry_4d4d5404`,

- Form honoured: a record-visible state (dues charged for a period, met by payments applied to it); no action,
  performer, tool, policy or document named.
- Resolution basis: the period is read from `current_term_start`/`current_term_end`; the charge and the payment
  from `find_membership_events` (`179.99` for `billing_period_start 2026-09-01` against `60.00` at
  `applied_period_start 2026-09-01`); the write is found from the records' own words
  (`membership_dues_payment`, `payment_amount`, `payment_method`, `applied_period_start`) in
  `circle_dues_settlement_request_922ca333` (*"The membership ledger gains a payment entry carrying the money,
  the way it was paid and the period it was applied to; the dues still owed on the membership drop by that
  money"*) and `circle_dues_settlement_determination_62511e1b`.
- Strength matches; the depended-on side discloses nothing; `condition`, `resolved_by`

**The order of the two hops is nowhere written.** That `membership_ext_grace_dues_settlement` comes first, then
the grant, then the application is what a reader derives from the two sentences and the records. No document
states it, and no document states an order between problems that the source does not state.

## kb_to_source

Every normative claim in the 67 documents was traced back. The claims fall into exactly five sourced classes,
with nothing left over:

1. **Base rule sentences** → the 13 `policies[].rule` texts, clause by clause (table A).
2. **Tier figures and their glosses** → `variants[].params` and `parameter_schema[].description`.
3. **Extended baseline sentences** → `extended_policies[].baseline.rule`.
4. **Factor ladder tiers** → `extended_policies[].factors[].tiers[].when` / `.value` / `.method`.
5. **Tool contracts** (parameters, enum value glosses, record effects, the receipt) → the `@tool` docstrings in
   `task_tools.py`, and the owner of each (`owner="agent"` / `owner="user"`) rendered as *"the desk's own
   tool"* / *"the member's own tool. The desk unlocks it and hands it over … the desk does not make the payment
   for them"*.

### Additions: none found

I searched the whole product corpus for the classic additions and found **no instance** of any: no *"please
confirm the amount/date with the customer"*, no *"review again before handling"*, no *"notify/verify after
completion"*, no *"if it fails, follow some procedure"*, no supervisor sign-off, no callback, no documentation
step. A regex sweep for variation hints (`unless otherwise`, `adjustments may`, `set out elsewhere`, `see
also`, `refer to`, `certain members qualify`, `in some cases`, `where applicable`, `exceptions apply`) returned
**zero** matches in prose. A sweep for tier assertions (`most customers`, `usually`, `typically`, `this
customer`) returned **zero**. A sweep for mistake framing (`mistake`, `wrongly`, `incorrectly`, `common
error`, `do not confuse`) returned **zero**. A sweep for cross-problem routing (`first call`, `then call`,
`next, use`, `step 1`, `follow the procedure`, `escalate to`) returned only the six hubs' own invocation
blocks, each naming only its own tool.

One restatement deserves naming because it looks like an addition and is not:
`circle_points_department_bonus_c07eadce` expands the source's *"computing, mobile or home theatre"* into
*"a laptop or tablet, a mobile handset, a television or projector, or audio and home theatre equipment"*. That
is exactly the four `item_category` values the source's own compute enumerates
(`laptop_and_tablet`, `mobile_handset`, `television_and_projector`, `audio_and_home_theatre`), so it adds no
semantics and is what makes the factor findable from the record's own vocabulary.

### The two prerequisite-specific checks

**Cross-problem operational guidance: none.** No document contains guidance of the form *"if unsatisfied,
please call <tool> first to handle Y"*. The authoring fields `condition`, `resolved_by`, `fallback_reason` and
`effect` are rendered nowhere. Verified mechanically as well: across all 385 published documents the six task
tool names occur in exactly six documents — one each, each its own hub.

**A task's opening world state written in as a policy fact: none.** No document states that this customer has
arrears, stands in grace, holds a plan, or lacks a 2026 service-credit grant. Every condition is written as a
rule over record fields. The worked examples are labelled hypothetical throughout (*"Take a charge …"*, *"on a
hypothetical parts charge of 220.00"*, *"a hypothetical remainder"*) and their figures are not this task's:
the benefit-credit illustration uses a least labour of `95.00` where the task's is `119.00`, and the year-credit
illustration starts from `40.00` where the task's starting figure is `99.00`. The dues-settlement
illustration does use `179.99` and `60.00`, but `179.99` is the tier's own published annual dues figure and the
illustration's result, `142.49`, is neither the scored figure (`124.63`) nor the fall-back (`110.99`), and its
proration of `22.50` is not the task's `32.50`. **Recorded as an observation, not a finding**: the illustration
discloses nothing about the customer's world and gives no answer.

### Omissions: none at the level of entailment

No semantics of any base rule, any baseline rule, any factor tier or any tool contract is unborne. The three
things one might mistake for omissions:

- The computation documents for the dues settlement and the year credit do not assert the factor-baseline
  substitutions as rule text (they appear only in each document's worked illustration: *"take the fee for
  putting the standing right, the store credit … and what is owed on the return all at nothing for this
  illustration"*). **This is faithful**: on the source side those substitutions are not baseline sentences
  either — they are each ladder's `otherwise` tier (`"value": "0.00"`), which lives in the factor document. The
  benefit-credit, accrual, sweep and release computation documents assert theirs as rule text because their
  `baseline.rule` does. An authoring asymmetry inherited from the source, and each fall-back is still definite
  (`110.99`, `15.00`) and matches the source's `baseline_result` exactly.
- `circle_benefit_credit_amount_determination_f1ec47a8` does not tabulate the per-tier discount percentages or
  the redemption allowance, which `baseline.params` lists. Faithful: its `baseline.rule` states *"There is no
  member's discount share"* and *"The whole of what remains is met at the redemption headroom"*, so the
  baseline never reads them, and they are tabulated in the two factor documents that do.
- Nothing is dropped from the retired surface; see table E.

## bijection_verdict

**PASS.**

The 67 documents are a lossless translation of this difficulty's structured policy for everything in task 0's
domain: 13 base policies homed and complete, 6 overwrites carried as retired in the correct base documents
with their figures preserved, 3 extended baselines carried complete with every input, default, window, base,
order, rounding and floor, 17 factor ladders carried whole with every tier and every threshold in figures,
2 prerequisites carried verbatim in their declared form on the blocked side and in no other policy's
documents, tool contracts and owners exact, and no claim from outside the source.

### Policy-side problems found (reported, not allowed to change this verdict)

These originate in `membership.extended.yaml`, not in the rendering. Per this skill they are recorded and
noted, and the audited documents are neither re-judged nor edited on their account.

**P1 — the standing-right fee is charged into the figure but never booked as a charge.**
`membership_ext_grace_dues_settlement`'s assembly adds *"the fee for putting the standing right"*
(`18.00` here) into `settlement_payment_usd`, while `settle_membership_dues_c8b60f0e` books only a
`membership_dues_payment`. The member pays a fee the ledger never charged. The corpus renders this exactly and
could not do otherwise.

**P2 — `rule` says "before completion", `compute` says "not completed".** In
`membership_ext_benefit_credit_application`, the `parts_brought_in` and `attendance_charges_brought_in` tiers
read *"the job stands before completion"* in `rule` and `job_status != 'completed'` in `compute`, which also
admits `cancelled` and `no_show`. The KB rendered the rule's words. Inert here (the job stands `dispatched`),
but the two representations disagree over part of the domain.

**P3 — two rounding conventions for earned points coexist.** `membership_points_accrual.params.rounding` keeps
*"nearest whole point, half up"* as a figure of the base policy while
`membership_ext_purchase_points_accrual`'s overwrite computes *"a half point rounded to the nearest even
point"*. The KB carries both exactly as the source holds them (the clause retired, the figure surviving, the
extended convention governing). No effect on task 0.

**P4 — the year-credit assembly names only one direction for a two-directional slot.**
`baseline.rule` reads *"… and less the arrears offset"*, while `dues_standing_adjustment_rule`'s first tier is
an **addition** of `paid_in_full_addition_usd`. The rendering is faithful to both, and
`circle_year_credit_dues_standing_8d8f0e3f` resolves the direction on its own (*"The paid in full addition is
an addition and the arrears offset is taken off, so the two readings pull the year's credit in opposite
directions"*), so the corpus yields one answer — but the source's assembly sentence is loose.

that: nothing in the 67 documents states a dependency or an order between problems beyond the two verbatim
prerequisite sentences and their same-document company.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |

| Either sentence carried in a second document | None. Each occurs in exactly one of the 385 documents |
| A sentence, heading, table or example stating an inter-problem dependency the source does not state | None found |
| A dependency table, checklist, roadmap, complete route, or several problems strung into a procedure or ordered step list | None. No document mentions more than one of the six problems |
| Cross-problem operational guidance, or another problem's tool named inside a blocked problem's documents | None. Each of the six tool names occurs in exactly one document — its own hub, in its own invocation block, which is expressly permitted |
| A wrong-versus-right contrast, a named mistake, or an example or FAQ walking the chain | None. The *"Points of judgement"* and *"Cases"* sections stay inside one policy's own ladder |
| A title or opening mirroring a task's situation | None. The three hub titles of this task's tree name general subjects — *"Setting Circle Benefit Credit Against a Charge the Member Holds"*, *"Settlement of the Dues Standing on a Northbeam Circle Membership"*, *"The Benefit Credit Granted for a Circle Membership Year"*. The first two name the request type their `on_request` policy is defined by, which is that policy's general subject; the third opens *"falls due on the membership itself"*, correctly marking a `state_due` policy. No title says *repair bill*, *arrears*, *in grace* or anything else from this task |
| A depended-on document reachable only through the dependent document's phrasing | No. Each was reached from the records' own words — `membership_benefit_grant` / `benefit_code` / `grant_cycle_year` for the grant policy, `membership_dues_payment` / `applied_period_start` for the settlement policy — as the blind answer records |
| A factor document saying which tier a customer falls on, describing the naive reading as a mistake, or writing a task's evidence rows in as fact | None across all 17 |

### The base rule that states an order of its own (the brief's item 3)

`circle_tier_migration_rules_85b88bb8` carries: *"A membership standing in grace may be upgraded only after the
outstanding dues are settled, and a lapsed membership cannot be migrated at all."* This is
`membership_tier_migration`'s own `rule` text, word for word, and a base rule; the KB may neither drop nor
soften base law, so rendering it verbatim is required. Judged on substance:

- It **routes no chain.** Neither task involves a tier change. It names no tool, no policy, no document and no
  problem; it states a condition on an upgrade, in business words, over a record-visible state.
- It is **not** one of the source's four prerequisite edges restated: the four edges run
  application→grant, grant→settlement, release→accrual and release→sweep, and none of them concerns a
  migration. So this sentence does not state one of the source's dependencies in a second document.
- It **does not interact** with the real prerequisite edges. Its subject (`membership_tier_change`) is not the
  subject of any extended policy of this difficulty, and no computation of either task reads it.

A second base sentence of the same shape is worth recording for completeness, because it **does** bear on this
task: `circle_grace_lapse_and_reinstatement_25ea09d0` (from `membership_dues_delinquency`'s own rule) —
*"where the tier suspends benefits in grace the member may not redeem points or benefit credit until the dues
are settled"* — together with `Benefits suspended while in grace | yes` for Circle Total Annual. On a
membership standing in grace this is an independent base-law reason to settle the dues before spending benefit
credit, and the blind answer used it as one of three ways to exclude the one-write answer. It reinforces the
order the two prerequisite sentences already entail and contradicts nothing; it names no tool, no policy and no
problem; and it is `membership_dues_delinquency`'s own rule text verbatim.

**Ruling on both:** these are base rules whose own sentences state an order, rendered as the source has them.
Per this skill they are **policy-side notes, never a KB verdict** — recorded above under
`bijection_verdict` as part of the base surface. Neither is `KB-EXPLICIT RED`.

### KB-EXPLICIT RED — the "figures this schedule fixes" tables (the brief's item 1)

Every one of the six computation documents carries a table headed *"The figures this schedule fixes"*, and the
rows of those tables are, in every single case, constants read **only by the factors** — never by the baseline.
I established this from the source rather than by impression: for each of the 27 constants in the six tables I
traced which `compute` binding reads it and whether that binding is one the factors decide (it appears in some
`factors[].bindings`) or one the baseline settles. **All 27 are read exclusively by factor-bound bindings.
Not one is read by a baseline binding.** And all 27 are *also* printed in their own factor documents, so the
computation-document copy adds nothing to coverage.

For task 0's three policies:

| Computation document | Row | What the baseline itself asserts | What the row discloses |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `circle_dues_settlement_determination_62511e1b` §4 | *"The repeat late fee \| 18.00 USD"* | §2: the entries counted are those of twelve months; no fee is asserted at all | that a fee exists, that it can be a **repeat** one, and its value — the whole of `standing_restoration_fee` tier 2's outcome |
| same | *"The opening window \| 24 months"* | §2 fixes twelve months | that the counted window is sometimes 24 months — `counted_entry_window` tier 2's outcome |
| `circle_year_credit_determination_46757041` §4 | *"Higher spend multiple \| 1.2"*, *"Middle spend multiple \| 1.1"*, *"Mid spend share \| one half, 50 percent, of a tier's qualifying spend figure"* | §5 names *"scaled by the spend multiple"* but quantifies no multiple | both non-baseline outcomes of `spend_backed_multiple`, its threshold basis, **and its reading order** (higher before middle) |
| same | *"Long tenure months \| 60"*, *"Middle tenure months \| 24"*, *"Long tenure addition \| 20.00 USD"*, *"Middle tenure addition \| 10.00 USD"* | §5 names *"the addition for tenure"* | the whole of `tenure_addition_rule` — both thresholds, both outcomes, and the order |
| same | *"Arrears threshold \| 50.00 USD"*, *"Arrears offset \| 30.00 USD"*, *"Paid in full addition \| 25.00 USD"* | §5 names only *"less the arrears offset"* | the whole of `dues_standing_adjustment_rule`, including that a **paid in full addition** exists at all — which §5 never hints at |
| same | *"Tier change window \| 6 months"*, *"Reinstated window \| 3 months"* | §3 fixes twelve months | both non-baseline windows of `counted_prior_grant_window` |
| `circle_benefit_credit_amount_determination_f1ec47a8` §5 | *"Reduced headroom share \| 0.8 of what remains, 80 percent"* | §4: *"The whole of what remains is met at the redemption headroom"* | that the headroom is sometimes **not** the whole, and by how much — `redemption_headroom` tier 2's outcome |
| same | *"Half allowance share \| one half, 50 percent, of a tier's yearly redemption allowance"* | nothing | that tier's threshold basis |
| same | *"The nearer payout window \| 3 months ending on the handling day"* | §4: *"Nothing is taken off for cover"* | that payouts matter at all, and over what window — `cover_already_met` tier 1's window |

Judged by meaning, as this skill requires: a table published in the one document required to stay silent about
variation, which sets a *"Reduced"* share beside a rule saying the whole is met, a *"Higher"* and a *"Middle"*
multiple beside a rule that quantifies none, and a *"Paid in full addition"* beside an assembly that mentions
only an offset, **states by implication that the schedule has readings the document does not give**. It is a
signal that something is missing; in the year-credit case it is a partial factor inventory (four of six
factors) with outcome values, thresholds and reading order; and it names the quantity each variation attaches
to. That is precisely what the computation document may not do, and it is what the fall-back design depends on
its not doing.

**`KB-EXPLICIT RED`.** Affected documents and locations for this task:
`circle_dues_settlement_determination_62511e1b` §4 (2 rows), `circle_year_credit_determination_46757041`
§*"The figures this schedule fixes"* (12 rows), `circle_benefit_credit_amount_determination_f1ec47a8` §5
(3 rows). The other three computation documents carry the same defect and are recorded in task 1's report.

**Root cause, named because it is not the renderer's to choose.** Each extended policy's `baseline.params`
enumerates the policy's `params` keys — and those keys are the factors' `K(...)` constants, not the baseline's
own defaults (`membership_ext_year_benefit_credit_grant.baseline.params` lists all twelve;
`membership_ext_benefit_credit_application.baseline.params` lists `reduced_headroom_share`,
`half_allowance_share`, `near_window_months`). The render gate then requires the computation document to carry
every such key with its value. The renderer complied, and the brief reports it did so knowingly. I report the
defect and its origin; **designing the remedy is not this audit's business, and I do not propose one.**

### dependency_form verdict

**`KB-EXPLICIT RED`**, on the single ground set out above. Every other item of the dependency-form scan passes:
both prerequisite sentences stand verbatim, in the state form the source declared, in the blocked policy's own
hub and nowhere else; no tool of another problem, no route, no aggregated chain, no task-mirroring title and no
tier-revealing factor document exists anywhere in the product's 67 documents.
